**Status:** production invention; repository starter contract.

The configured production id is this starter's repository identity and temporary working title. The package delivers a deterministic film blocking pass, not a direct brief or reusable-only library. Its authored ladder ends in two six-second screenplay sources whose half-second dissolve produces an 11.5-second final timeline.

Required output consists of a deterministic preview, a deterministic feature, one pose guide pass, English accessibility captions, and a zero-gain audio mix whose only source is an inert structural pipeline fixture. Delivery ends after the terminal answer hold and its fade to black. A production whose complete intent fits one non-narrative observation instead selects `brief`; one that delivers reusable design and source without shots selects `library`.

**Status:** production invention; repository starter contract.

The logline is: “A soloist raises a hand, and a chorus standing in rows answers it.” Every lower-layer tradeoff preserves one readable call-and-response: SOLOIST's raised hand is the call, CHORUS's ordered 2 m advance is the answer, and the held relation proves that answer was received. Detail that does not strengthen that observation or its deterministic verification is outside the starter.

**Status:** production invention; repository starter contract.

The audience receives only external audiovisual evidence selected by the screenplay and realized by reviewed shots: staged bodies, formation relations, the gate, the plaza, transitions, an accessibility caption, and deliberate silence. No private thought, narrator, dialogue, or off-screen causal fact is available. Cuts and dissolves may move between unequal-scale observations without implying that subjects moved between shots. The audience first sees an ambiguous raised-hand action, then may infer that it was an addressed cue only when the ordered formation visibly answers.

**Status:** production invention; repository starter contract.

English is the primary working language of authored production documents and the audience-facing accessibility caption. Exact code identifiers, numeric records, and standards terminology retain their declared forms. This starter authors no spoken or secondary language; adding one requires settings to define audience access and the screenplay to define its visible or audible content.

**Status:** production invention; repository convention.

All distances are metres and all durations are seconds. The world is right-handed with positive Y up, and `plaza-center` is the ground-level origin. Formation and model-local frames declare their relation to this shared frame instead of redefining it. These are chosen repository conventions, not measurements of an external place.

**Status:** derived; literal audit of the starter's declared delivery.

Production identity, output shape, runtime, governing aim, recipient access, language, units, and time are authored in this file. SOLOIST, CHORUS, GATE, PLAZA, and the visual and audible grammar have dedicated settings owners. Their capabilities, relations, initial states, limits, and delivery observations are explicit before model, motion, or narrative selection.

The starter inherits ordinary daylight, gravity, and human-scale spatial expectations except where a setting states a deliberate departure. It claims no external history, institution, economy, dialogue system, private psychology, resource network, hazard, wall, room, weather simulation, or event before the opening. Those domains are outside this delivery rather than unresolved. No unresolved settings decision is permitted to reach a downstream layer; a newly required domain must receive its own H2 owner here before that layer resumes.
